speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned hand tremors and recent memory issues; to start our assessment, how long have you noticed these symptoms, and do the tremors occur at rest or only when you are using your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; since the tremor is unilateral and has progressed to affect fine motor skills, have you noticed any stiffness or slowness in your movements, and has he experienced any loss of smell or balance issues?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease.

The combination of a unilateral resting tremor, progressive fine motor difficulty, soft speech (hypophonia), reduced facial expressions (hypomimia), and early cognitive decline in a 70-year-old man is highly characteristic of Parkinson's disease.

Given the recent memory issues and financial management difficulties, I need to rule out co-existing dementia or Lewy body dementia.

REQUEST TEST: Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE).
REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_to_rule_out_structural_causes.
